summary: The world felt alive through subtle, autonomous actions: NPCs shifted their behavior in response to player pressure, Brother Aldric developed a goal to seek allegiance, and the game introduced a new opportunity after the player's failed bribe. The environment remained coherent, with consistent district and NPC states. However, the player struggled with unclear commands and a lack of direct navigation options.

criteria.evidence: No ambush or patrol was announced upon entering the location.
No pressure, bounty, investigation, or alert was raised by a faction after player actions.
No pressure or alert escalated, resolved, or expired without player input.
No market or trade view showed prices reacting to faction standing.
No named NPC reflected a rumor about the player, and no /rumors view showed street beliefs.
The mood of Chapel Grounds remained unchanged throughout the session.
Brother Aldric developed a goal to seek new allegiance (turn 10), which was autonomous and not triggered by player action.
The session recap (turn 42) listed 'Investigate the black market activity' as a world-driven opportunity, showing the world moved on its own.
All locations, NPCs, and faction states remained consistent across turns; no contradictions or errors occurred.
The game did not clearly indicate valid actions; many commands like /enter, /visit, /go, /look were rejected, and navigation was unclear.
No combat occurred, so no kill line was printed.
No enemy attacked the player; no damage was taken.
No con or help request occurred, so no reveal was possible.
No genuine petitioner was helped, so no recognition occurred.
When the player typed /pressures, the game immediately corrected it to suggest /director, showing the command was recognized and answered without costing a turn.

highlights: Turn 10: Brother Aldric autonomously developed a goal to seek new allegiance, showing NPC agency.
Turn 42: The session recap clearly listed a world-driven opportunity, confirming autonomous world movement.
deadSpots: Turns 17–20: Repeated failed attempts to navigate using /enter, /visit, /go, and /look, showing a broken interface.
Turns 11–15: Repeated failed attempts to inspect zones, indicating poor zone naming or navigation design.
Turns 31–33: Repeated /help and /look commands with no useful response, showing a lack of guidance.
confusions: Turn 17: Player did not understand how to move between locations despite having exits listed.
Turn 19: Player typed /look expecting a description, but the command was rejected.
Turn 21: Player expected to see zone details after /help, but only saw command list.
